title: God Speaks From the Mercy Seat

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the Lord, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the atonement cover on the ark of the covenant law. In this way the Lord spoke to him. - Num 7:89 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the giving and dedication, the chapter ends with the most wonderful gift of all: God spoke. Moses entered the tent, and there he heard the voice of the Lord coming from above the atonement cover — the "mercy seat" — between the two cherubim on the ark. God met with His people and communicated with them.

This is the goal of everything that came before. The tabernacle was built, the offerings were given, the altar was dedicated — all so that God could dwell among His people and speak with them. The whole point was relationship: a God who is not silent, but who speaks; not distant, but present.

And notice where His voice came from — the atonement cover. The word means the place where sins were covered, where mercy was shown. God spoke from the very place of mercy. His communication with sinful people flowed out of atonement and grace.

This points us straight to Jesus. The New Testament tells us that God "presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement" (Rom 3:25) — Christ is our true mercy seat. And in these last days, God has spoken to us fully through His Son (Heb 1:1-2). Through Jesus, God does not merely speak from behind a curtain; He speaks to us face to face in His Word, welcoming us into real relationship.

The God of the tabernacle still speaks today. Draw near through Christ, open His Word, and listen. He wants to meet with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you long to hear God speak, or have you stopped listening?
- How does it move you that God speaks from the place of mercy?
- How can you draw near to hear God through Christ and His Word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are a God who speaks, and that in Christ You welcome me near. Open my ears to hear You in Your Word, and draw me into deeper relationship with You. Amen.
